subject: B
topic: All topics of GK & Current Affairs India (mixed)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the founder of the Maurya dynasty?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya dynasty around 322 BCE with the guidance of Chanakya. Bindusara and Ashoka were his son and grandson respectively, later rulers of the same dynasty, and Chanakya was the political mentor, not a ruler, so only Chandragupta Maurya is the founder.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian rivers:

(i) The Yamuna is a tributary of the Ganga.
(ii) The Godavari originates in Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra.
(iii) The Krishna river empties into the Arabian Sea.
(iv) The Brahmaputra is known as Tsangpo in Tibet.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Yamuna joins the Ganga at Prayagraj, the Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar, and the Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo in Tibet, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are true. Statement (iii) is false because the Krishna flows east into the Bay of Bengal, not the Arabian Sea, so any option including (iii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Green Revolution' in India is primarily associated with the increased production of:
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution in the 1960s boosted foodgrain output, especially wheat and rice, using high-yielding varieties. Milk is linked to the White Revolution, fish to the Blue Revolution, and cotton to the Fibre Revolution, so none of them is the Green Revolution focus; wheat and rice are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following freedom fighters with their movements:

Column I:
(a) Vinoba Bhave
(b) Subhas Chandra Bose
(c) Bhagat Singh
(d) Mahatma Gandhi

Column II:
(i) Salt Satyagraha
(ii) Bhoodan Movement
(iii) Hindustan Socialist Republican Association
(iv) Indian National Army

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Vinoba Bhave led the Bhoodan Movement, Bose formed the INA, Bhagat Singh was part of the HSRA, and Gandhi led the Salt Satyagraha, giving (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(i). The other options swap Bhoodan with INA or misplace HSRA and Salt Satyagraha, which are historically incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Sabarmati Ashram is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Sabarmati Ashram, founded by Gandhi in 1917, stands on the banks of the Sabarmati river in Ahmedabad. Wardha and Sevagram host other Gandhian ashrams, and Pune has no Sabarmati Ashram, so Ahmedabad is the correct location.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are important documents of Indian democracy?

(i) The Constitution
(ii) The Preamble
(iii) The Fundamental Rights
(iv) The Manusmriti

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Constitution, its Preamble and the Fundamental Rights (Part III) are foundational to Indian democracy, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. The Manusmriti is an ancient text and not a document of Indian democracy, so any option including it is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Mother Teresa in the year:
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her humanitarian work with the poor. 1975 and 1977 predate her award, and 1985 is later, so none of them matches; 1979 is the correct year.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is a member of BRICS.
Reason (R): BRICS stands for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: India is a member of BRICS, and BRICS is the acronym for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. India's presence in the letter 'I' of the acronym is exactly what makes it a member, so (R) correctly explains (A). Other options fail because both statements are true and (R) explains (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is India's National Song?
questions.explanation: 'Vande Mataram', from Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's Anandamath, is India's National Song. 'Jana Gana Mana' is the National Anthem, 'Saare Jahan Se Achha' is a patriotic poem by Iqbal, and 'Ae Mere Watan Ke Logon' is a patriotic song, so none of them is the National Song; Vande Mataram is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian Prime Ministers:

(i) Jawaharlal Nehru served the longest as Prime Minister.
(ii) Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan'.
(iii) Manmohan Singh was an economist before becoming Prime Minister.
(iv) Atal Bihari Vajpayee was India's first Prime Minister.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Nehru served longest as PM, Shastri coined 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan', and Manmohan Singh was an economist before becoming PM, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because Nehru was India's first PM, not Vajpayee, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The National Emblem of India is adapted from the:
questions.explanation: India's National Emblem is adapted from Ashoka's Lion Capital at Sarnath, showing four Asiatic lions. The Sanchi Stupa is a Buddhist monument, the Ajanta Caves are famous for murals, and the Konark Sun Temple is a Hindu temple, none of which is the source of the National Emblem, so Sarnath is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows India's tea production (in thousand tonnes):

2019 — 1350
2020 — 1250
2021 — 1330
2022 — 1370

In which year was tea production the lowest?
questions.explanation: In 2020, production dropped to 1250 thousand tonnes, the lowest of the four years. 2021 and 2019 recorded higher figures at 1330 and 1350, and 2022 was the highest at 1370, so none of them is lower than 2020, which is the correct year.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who wrote the book 'The Discovery of India'?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort (1942–46). Gandhi wrote 'My Experiments with Truth', Sardar Patel was not a major book author of that title, and Rajendra Prasad wrote 'India Divided', so only Nehru authored 'The Discovery of India'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following states with their capitals:

Column I:
(a) Odisha
(b) Assam
(c) Gujarat
(d) Kerala

Column II:
(i) Gandhinagar
(ii) Thiruvananthapuram
(iii) Bhubaneswar
(iv) Dispur

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The capitals are Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Dispur (Assam), Gandhinagar (Gujarat) and Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala), giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii). The other options swap Dispur with Gandhinagar or misplace the Kerala capital, which do not match the actual state capitals.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Reserve Bank of India was established in the year:
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India was set up on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934. 1925 and 1930 predate its establishment, and 1947 is the year of Indian independence, not the year the RBI began, so only 1935 is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are official languages of the United Nations?

(i) English
(ii) French
(iii) Hindi
(iv) Russian

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: English, French and Russian are three of the six UN official languages (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish), so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Hindi, though widely spoken, is not a UN official language, so any option including Hindi is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Kabini river is a tributary of which major river?
questions.explanation: The Kabini rises in Kerala and joins the Cauvery in Karnataka, making it a tributary of the Cauvery. The Krishna, Godavari and Narmada have their own tributary systems and do not include the Kabini, so only the Cauvery is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body.
Reason (R): The Election Commission conducts elections to the Panchayats.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: The assertion is true: the Election Commission of India is established under Article 324 of the Constitution. However, elections to Panchayats are conducted by the State Election Commissions, not the ECI, so the reason is false. Hence (A) is correct but (R) is wrong; the first two options fail because (R) is false, and the last fails because (A) is true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Meghdoot' operation launched by India in 1984 was related to which region?
questions.explanation: Operation Meghdoot was India's 1984 military operation to secure the Siachen Glacier. The Rann of Kutch, Sundarbans and Aksai Chin are all significant but were not the target of Meghdoot, so only Siachen is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Chief Minister of a state is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: Under Article 164, the Governor appoints the Chief Minister of a state, usually the leader of the majority party. The President appoints the PM at the Centre, the PM does not appoint state CMs, and the Chief Justice heads the judiciary rather than making executive appointments, so only the Governor is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian agriculture:

(i) India is one of the largest producers of milk in the world.
(ii) Punjab is famous for its wheat production.
(iii) Kerala is a major producer of rubber and coconut.
(iv) India does not grow tea commercially.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: India is a top milk producer, Punjab is famed for wheat, and Kerala produces rubber and coconut, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because India is a major tea producer, especially in Assam and West Bengal, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the largest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan, at about 3.42 lakh sq km, is the largest Indian state by area. Madhya Pradesh is second, Maharashtra third and Uttar Pradesh fourth, so none of them exceeds Rajasthan's area, making Rajasthan the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Article 370' of the Indian Constitution was related to the special status of:
questions.explanation: Article 370 granted a special autonomous status to Jammu & Kashmir until its abrogation in August 2019. Nagaland has special provisions under Article 371A, Sikkim under 371F, and Manipur has other provisions, but none of them was governed by Article 370, so only J&K is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following personalities with their contributions:

Column I:
(a) Homi Bhabha
(b) Vikram Sarabhai
(c) M.S. Swaminathan
(d) Verghese Kurien

Column II:
(i) Space research
(ii) Green Revolution
(iii) Atomic energy
(iv) White Revolution

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Homi Bhabha pioneered atomic energy, Vikram Sarabhai founded space research, M.S. Swaminathan led the Green Revolution, and Verghese Kurien led the White Revolution, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv). The other options swap atomic energy with space or misplace the two revolutions, which are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Jaipur foot' is an example of:
questions.explanation: The Jaipur foot is a low-cost, rubber-based prosthetic leg developed in India for amputees. It is not a dance, instrument or hill station; the name reflects its origin in Jaipur but the object itself is a prosthetic limb, so that is the correct description.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India?

(i) Taj Mahal
(ii) Qutub Minar
(iii) India Gate
(iv) Ajanta Caves

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar and Ajanta Caves are all UNESCO World Heritage Sites, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. India Gate is a war memorial in Delhi but is not listed as a UNESCO Heritage Site, so any option including India Gate is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is in:
questions.explanation: The WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. New York hosts the UN headquarters, Paris hosts UNESCO, and Vienna hosts the IAEA, so none of them houses the WHO, making Geneva the correct city.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is the largest democracy in the world.
Reason (R): India has the largest population in the world.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: India is the world's largest democracy, and it has the largest population. A country is called the largest democracy when it has the biggest electorate, so having the largest population is precisely why India earns that title, and (R) correctly explains (A). Other options fail because both statements are true and (R) explains (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Indian rupee symbol '₹' was officially adopted in the year __________.
questions.explanation: The Indian government adopted the '₹' symbol in July 2010, designed by D. Udaya Kumar. 2005 predates its adoption, and 2012 and 2015 come after, so none of them is the year of adoption; 2010 is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the number of new startups recognised by DPIIT in India:

2019 — 8600
2020 — 15000
2021 — 20000
2022 — 26500

What is the total number of startups recognised over these four years?
questions.explanation: Total = 8600 + 15000 + 20000 + 26500 = 70,100. Option 55000, 60000 and 68000 all fall short of this sum by different amounts arising from dropping or misreading a value, so only 70100 correctly totals the four annual counts.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Blue Revolution' in India is related to:
questions.explanation: The Blue Revolution refers to the rapid growth of fisheries and aquaculture in India. The White Revolution is about milk, the Fibre Revolution about cotton, and the Yellow Revolution about oilseeds, so none of them fits 'Blue'; fish production is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Armed Forces:

(i) The President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.
(ii) The Indian Army, Navy and Air Force are the three main branches.
(iii) The National Cadet Corps (NCC) is a youth wing of the Indian Armed Forces.
(iv) The Indian Army has never sent troops on UN peacekeeping missions.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The President is the Supreme Commander, the three services are the Army, Navy and Air Force, and NCC is a youth training organisation linked to the armed forces, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because India has been a major contributor to UN peacekeeping missions, so any option with (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following folk dances with their states:

Column I:
(a) Bhangra
(b) Garba
(c) Bihu
(d) Kathakali

Column II:
(i) Gujarat
(ii) Assam
(iii) Punjab
(iv) Kerala

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bhangra is from Punjab, Garba from Gujarat, Bihu from Assam and Kathakali from Kerala, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv). The other options swap Punjab with Gujarat or Assam with Kerala, which do not match each dance's home state.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which body prepares the Union Budget of India?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget is prepared by the Ministry of Finance, specifically the Department of Economic Affairs. The Home Ministry handles internal security, NITI Aayog is a think tank, and the RBI manages monetary policy, so none of them prepares the Budget, making the Finance Ministry correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian classical music:

(i) Hindustani and Carnatic are its two main streams.
(ii) Sitar and tabla are instruments used in Hindustani music.
(iii) Ravi Shankar was a famous sitar maestro.
(iv) Bharatanatyam is a form of classical music.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hindustani and Carnatic are the two main classical streams, sitar and tabla are Hindustani instruments, and Ravi Shankar was a legendary sitarist, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form, not a music genre, so any option with (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Tarapur Atomic Power Station is located in the state of:
questions.explanation: The Tarapur Atomic Power Station, India's first commercial nuclear plant, is at Tarapur in Maharashtra. Gujarat hosts Kakrapar, Rajasthan hosts the Rawatbhata plant, and Tamil Nadu hosts Kalpakkam and Kudankulam, so none of them houses Tarapur, making Maharashtra correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Chipko Movement' was launched to protect:
questions.explanation: The Chipko Movement of the 1970s in Uttarakhand aimed to prevent tree-felling and protect forests by villagers hugging trees. Rivers were the focus of movements like Narmada Bachao, wildlife has separate conservation programmes, and wetlands are protected under Ramsar rules, so forests are the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Supreme Court of India has original jurisdiction in disputes between states.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court of India is located in New Delhi.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Supreme Court has original jurisdiction in inter-state disputes under Article 131, and it is located in New Delhi. However, the Court's location is unrelated to its jurisdiction (which is granted by the Constitution), so (R) does not correctly explain (A). Other options fail because both statements are true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The city known as the 'Silicon Valley of India' is:
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is called the 'Silicon Valley of India' for its large IT industry and startups. Hyderabad is 'Cyberabad' with major IT presence, Chennai and Pune are also IT hubs, but the specific 'Silicon Valley' epithet belongs to Bengaluru, so it is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian National Anthem:

(i) It was written by Rabindranath Tagore.
(ii) It was originally in Bengali.
(iii) It was adopted as the National Anthem in 1950.
(iv) Its official duration of playing is about 82 seconds.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Tagore wrote the National Anthem originally in Bengali, and it was adopted on 24 January 1950, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the full official duration of the Anthem is about 52 seconds, not 82, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra involves a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash located in:
questions.explanation: Mount Kailash lies in Tibet, an autonomous region of China, and pilgrims from India cross the border to visit it. Nepal, Bhutan and India host their own sacred peaks but not Kailash itself, so 'Tibet (China)' is the correct location.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Duties:

(i) They are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution.
(ii) They were added by the 42nd Amendment.
(iii) There are ten Fundamental Duties.
(iv) They are directly enforceable in a court of law.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are in Part IV-A (Article 51A), were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), and are ten in number as originally enacted, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because they are not directly enforceable in courts, unlike Fundamental Rights, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Ramsar sites (wetlands of international importance) in India?

(i) Chilika Lake
(ii) Loktak Lake
(iii) Mount Abu
(iv) Sambhar Lake

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Chilika (Odisha), Loktak (Manipur) and Sambhar (Rajasthan) lakes are all Ramsar sites, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Mount Abu is a hill station in Rajasthan, not a wetland, so it is not a Ramsar site and any option that includes Mount Abu is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The largest tribal community in India is the:
questions.explanation: According to Census figures, the Bhils form the largest tribal community in India, spread across central and western states. The Gonds are second, the Santhals third, and the Mundas smaller, so none of them exceeds the Bhils in size, making 'Bhil' the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The 'GST' introduced in India in 2017 stands for __________.
questions.explanation: GST expands to Goods and Services Tax, a unified indirect tax that replaced many earlier taxes in 2017. 'General Sales Tax', 'Government Service Tax' and 'Gross State Tax' are not the correct expansions, so only 'Goods and Services Tax' fits the abbreviation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the highest gallantry award of India?
questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest wartime gallantry award. The Ashok Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry decoration, the Vir Chakra ranks lower than the PVC in wartime, and the Kirti Chakra is a peacetime award ranking below the Ashok Chakra, so the PVC is the top gallantry honour.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian Presidents:

(i) Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India.
(ii) A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was known as the 'People's President'.
(iii) Pratibha Patil was the first woman President of India.
(iv) Presidents in India are elected for a term of six years.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad was the first President, Kalam was called the People's President, and Pratibha Patil was the first woman President, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the President's term is five years, not six, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is a secular state.
Reason (R): The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India as sovereign, socialist, secular and democratic republic.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: India is a secular state, and its Preamble explicitly describes India as sovereign, socialist, secular and democratic. The Preamble's declaration is precisely what establishes the secular character, so (R) correctly explains (A). Other options fail because both statements are true and (R) does explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands are located in the:
questions.explanation: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal, east of the Indian mainland. The Lakshadweep Islands are in the Arabian Sea (Lakshadweep Sea) off the west coast, and the Palk Strait region lies between India and Sri Lanka, so none of those matches Andaman & Nicobar; the Bay of Bengal is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Space Programme:

(i) ISRO was formed in 1969.
(ii) Aryabhata was India's first satellite.
(iii) Chandrayaan-1 was launched in 2008.
(iv) India's first satellite was launched from Sriharikota.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ISRO was formed in 1969, Aryabhata (1975) was India's first satellite, and Chandrayaan-1 was launched in 2008, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because Aryabhata was launched from the Soviet cosmodrome Kapustin Yar, not from Sriharikota, so any option including (iv) is wrong.
